articles.title_orig: iOS 27.3 brings Apple Intelligence features to China
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.3 brings Apple Intelligence features to China
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27.3 beta 1 is here , and it includes the first Apple Intelligence features in China. Siri AI isn’t available yet, but a lot of other capabilities are. Here’s what to expect.
For the first time, Apple Intelligence is now available in China for beta users.
Apple Intelligence launched in the US in October 2024, so users in China have had to wait more than two years for the features to arrive.
But today with iOS 27.3 beta 1, like was announced last week , Apple Intelligence is officially available in China too.
Not all of Apple’s AI capabilities are here yet. Siri AI, notably, is missing. However, Apple outlines a wide array of AI features debuting in China with iOS 27.3.
Here’s the full list, via Apple Newsroom’s post :
Essentially, none of the new AI capabilities introduced in iOS 27 are included. Rather, Apple is focusing first on bringing the AI features from iOS 26 and iOS 18 to users in China.

articles.title_orig: Shopify Stock Falls as Slowing Merchandise Sales Flash a Warning Sign
articles.title_zh: Shopify Stock Falls as Slowing Merchandise Sales Flash a Warning Sign
articles.content_orig:
Shares of e-commerce platform Shopify fell 7% on Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gross profit and gross merchandise volume.
Shopify reported before the bell Tuesday and posted adjusted earnings of 49 cents per share, topping LSEG estimates of 46 cents per share.
Overall, quarterly revenue of $3.74 billion came in just below LSEG estimates of $3.75 billion. Shopify said it sees revenue growth in the "low thirties" range year over year for the fourth quarter, versus LSEG estimates of 32.1%.
Gross merchandise volume, which came in at $119.15 billion, missed analyst estimates of $120.03 billion for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Subscription gross profit also missed estimates by nearly $20 million, coming in at $661 million compared to StreetAccount estimates of $680.3 million. Merchant gross profit beat estimates.
Shopify president Harley Finkelstein called the GMV results "consistent" and "durable" in comments to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday, and noted it was the thirteenth consecutive quarter of GMV growth above 20%.
"We're really proud of the print, and we're going to keep building for the long term and ignore the noise day to day," Finkelstein said.
Subscription revenue of $836 million also missed analyst estimates of $848.1 million, according to FactSet. Merchant revenue beat estimates.
Meta released its consumer-facing artificial intelligence agent Muse during the third quarter, and Shopify was an early partner. The partnership allows Muse to browse and purchase items on Shopify's platform within the Muse app and allows customers to check out with Shopify's payment service, Shop Pay.
Finkelstein addressed concerns about potential pricing pressure as AI agents negotiate prices and cost compare on behalf of users.
"We're not seeing that prices are being lowered," he said.
Instead, Finkelstein said AI agents are driving new traffic to Shopify's business and are helping consumers find new brands and products. "Brands like the Tin Can phone, a screenless phone for kids, are seeing incredible success because of agentic-based commerce, where a consumer is being very specific and using very merit-based results and using Shopify catalog. It is presenting these great products to consumers that there's no way they would have found otherwise."
Finkelstein acknowledged some economic pressure on consumers heading into the holiday season, but said businesses are optimistic and agentic shopping could have a breakthrough moment.
"I do think this is the first holiday season where AI-assisted shopping capabilities will become mainstream, especially with the rise of personal agents," he said.

articles.title_orig: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.title_zh: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.content_orig:
Millions of Americans will be casting their votes in person in the 2026 midterm election on Tuesday, Nov. 3.
Polling times vary by state. States will begin reporting election results after their polls close.
Forty-seven states and the District of Columbia offer early voting options, with the exception of Alabama, Mississippi and New Hampshire. Eight states and Washington, D.C., automatically send a mail-in ballot to every registered voter, although voters generally can still choose to vote in person. Over 57 million voters have already cast their ballots early this year.
If you are in line to cast your ballot before a site closes, you have the right to remain in line and vote. View a list of voter rights from the ACLU here .
The first polls close at 6 p.m. ET in the eastern parts of Indiana and Kentucky. Then at 7 p.m., polls close in Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont and Virginia, the rest of Indiana, Kentucky and most of Florida. Then North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia follow at 7:30 p.m.

articles.title_orig: US job openings jump in September; layoffs lowest in 1-1/2 years
articles.title_zh: US job openings jump in September; layoffs lowest in 1-1/2 years
articles.content_orig:
Job openings surged in September, as did the number of workers who quit their positions, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday, while hiring also rose and layoffs dropped.
In its monthly look at labor market slack and worker mobility, the BLS reported job openings at 7.52 million, up 333,000 from August and well above the Dow Jones consensus outlook for 7.15 million.
As a share of the total workforce, the rate of job openings increased to 4.5%, up 0.2 percentage point from the prior month, according to the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey . There are now some 414,000 more job openings than workers classified as unemployed, or about 1.05 openings to every available worker.
Openings rose in manufacturing (54,000) as well as state and local government (108,000) and professional and business services (106,000).
At the same time, the total of employees leaving their jobs spiked to 3.36 million, an increase of 321,000 from August and the highest level since March 2025. Quits are considered a barometer for worker confidence in finding new jobs after leaving their prior positions.
"There are more job openings than unemployed people in the United States right now. That doesn't solve all problems, but it's a big change from a year ago," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "It's an encouraging sign that despite all the headwinds right now with high diesel and gas prices and ongoing inflation problems, companies are slowly increasing their hiring."
Hires rose on the month, up 131,000 to 5.4 million, while layoffs and discharges fell by 127,000 to 1.64 million, the lowest since March 2025.
The report comes ahead of the October nonfarm payrolls report, which the BLS will release Friday. The Wall Street consensus is for an increase of 59,000 after September eked out a gain of just 29,000, while the unemployment rate is figured to hold at 4.2%.
In other economic news Tuesday, September factory orders for manufactured goods jumped 1.8%, well above the estimate for 1.3% after increasing just 0.3% in August.

articles.title_orig: Google to shut off search for schools that opt-out of AI
articles.title_zh: Google to shut off search for schools that opt-out of AI
articles.content_orig:
Google announced Tuesday morning that it would switch off AI products by default for students in schools that use the technology giant’s education software. But those schools that forgo its AI services would also be cut off from Google Search.
The move comes after mounting criticism from advocacy groups and senators about the spread of Google’s AI services available in classrooms. Until Tuesday, its AI products — branded under the Gemini moniker — were automatically activated for schools using Google Classroom.
Google said Tuesday’s move would also cut off students’ access to Google Search if schools do not enable Gemini, given AI’s growing integration into the company’s search products.
Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post announcing the change that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search “will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.”
“We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach,” Phillips wrote.
Some education and technology advocates immediately slammed the decision, painting the move as a punishment for schools that don’t use Google’s AI. “It is unfortunate that Google has prioritized its business interests over the education of our children,” said Randi Weingarten, president of the American Federation of Teachers, a national educators union.
“Instead of working with teachers and parents to uphold privacy and ensure their tools are safe and useful, it throws the baby out with the bathwater and bans access to the tools altogether,” she told NBC News in written comments.
Josh Golin, executive director of advocacy group Fairplay, said in a statement that Google is attempting “to strong-arm schools into using its AI products.”
“Schools should use this opportunity to help students find more privacy-protective alternatives for search, as well as ways to do more substantive research beyond search and click,” Golin said.
Earlier this year, Google turned on Gemini in its Classroom app, allowing children — regardless of age — to access AI products unless districts disabled it .
Parent advocacy groups and experts on the use of technology in schools denounced Google for providing AI products to children — raising concern that students would outsource their work to AI systems on school devices — and lobbied school districts to disable Gemini products. In an open letter in early October, 13 leading parent advocacy organizations — including the Digital Childhood Institute and Schools Beyond Screens — called on school districts to turn off access to Gemini and YouTube, which is also owned by Google .
Google has established a dominant role in education technology over the past 15 years. The vast majority of Chromebook laptops are purchased by school districts to provide to students. Nearly two-thirds of assignments use a Google product, according to a 2023 report by the firm Schoolytics. This year, the company began offering multiday AI trainings for educators, featuring sessions that focused on how they could mitigate pushback by teachers who don’t want to use AI.
Research on AI in educational settings has not established a long-term benefit for students. There are no high-quality causal studies into student use of AI, according to the SCALE Initiative at the Stanford Graduate School of Education . Researchers have also warned that many of the studies conducted so far on AI in education didn’t measure whether it boosted learning and often did not test whether AI-assisted learning was superior to other teaching methods.
In Tuesday’s blog post , Google said that for schools that enable the company’s AI products, they will now detect when a student is trying to use them just to get an answer on an assignment. A redesigned version of Google Search will instead walk students through the topic or problem and work through the concepts, without going directly to the answer, the company said.
Jared Perlo is a technology reporter focused on AI for NBC News Digital.
Tyler Kingkade is a national reporter for NBC News, based in Los Angeles.

articles.title_orig: Former Weil partners lawyer up over firm’s wind-down
articles.title_zh: Former Weil partners lawyer up over firm’s wind-down
articles.content_orig:
Add Boston.com as your preferred source on Google to see more of our stories.
Just months after expanding into a new Back Bay office, international law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges is preparing to wind down — leaving the future uncertain for about 50 attorneys and staff members based in Boston.
News outlets have reported that leaders at the firm recommended an “orderly wind-down” last week after an exodus of high-earning partners and unsuccessful merger talks. The Wall Street Journal reports that the proposal remains subject to a vote by the firm’s partners.
The recommended wind-down comes less than five months after Weil opened a more than 37,000-square-foot office at Lyrik Back Bay, expanding its Boston footprint by one-third. The firm occupies two floors at 1001 Boylston St.
“Our move to this new, signature space in Boston marks a significant milestone and underscores the importance of this key market to our clients, our lawyers and the firm’s long-term strategy,” Weil Executive Partner Barry Wolf said when the office opened June 15 .
The building also houses CarGurus’ global headquarters and LEGO’s Boston office.
The wind-down would affect 39 attorneys and 13 staff members in Boston, according to a Boston Business Journal survey . Weil’s website currently lists 43 people associated with the Boston office.
Weil did not respond to a request for comment seeking confirmation on the number of affected employees or information about what would happen to its newly leased office space.
Weil established its Boston office in 2002. Since January 2025, the firm has added seven partners to the office, including six lateral hires and one internal promotion.
Founded in 1931, Weil has approximately 1,200 lawyers across three continents.
According to The American Lawyer’s 2026 Am Law 100, Weil was the 29th-highest-grossing U.S. law firm , generating nearly $2.1 billion in revenue in 2025. Locally, its Boston office ranked 65th among Massachusetts law firms by attorney headcount, according to Boston Business Journal .
Beth Treffeisen is a general assignment reporter for Boston.com, focusing on local news, crime, and business in the New England region.

articles.title_orig: Beijing launches diplomatic flurry amid threat of renewed U.S. war with Iran
articles.title_zh: Beijing launches diplomatic flurry amid threat of renewed U.S. war with Iran
articles.content_orig:
Beijing launches diplomatic salvo to woo Gulf leaders and bolster its influence in the region
China has held a flurry of meetings with Gulf leaders in a sign that Beijing is stepping up its diplomatic efforts in the Middle East.
The diplomatic salvo comes before a highly anticipated meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping when the US president is expected to attend the Apec conference in Shenzhen, China, on 18 and 19 November.
Xi held talks with Haitham bin Tariq , Oman’s sultan, in a historic state visit to Beijing on Monday.
President Xi’s foreign minister, Wang Yi, met Saudi Arabia’s national security adviser, Musaad bin Mohammed Al Aiban, and the deputy secretary of Iran’s national security council, Ali Bagheri Kani.
Haitham’s trip to Beijing is the first time that an Omani head of state has visited China since the two countries established diplomatic relations nearly 50 years ago. According to a Chinese readout of the meeting, Xi warned that the Middle East should not become an arena for “great power rivalry and geopolitical conflicts”.
He said: “China has always been actively committed to stopping conflict and promoting peace, and hopes to contribute wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security dilemma.”
Wang said after his separate talks that China was willing to “play a constructive role in helping the region emerge from the shadow of the pandemic and achieve lasting peace and stability”. In his meeting with Bagheri Kani, Wang said China supported Iran “in safeguarding its sovereignty and security”. According to China, the Iranian official said his country looked forward to China “playing a more important role in international and regional peace”.
When the US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February, China was credited with pushing Tehran toward ceasefire talks in Pakistan , bolstering its status as a regional mediator.
Beijing’s influence in the Middle East is “no longer what it used to be”, said Shen Dingli, a Shanghai-based scholar of international relations. But he added: “Given China’s increased investment and trade in the region … its influence cannot be ignored.”
As the war has dragged on, China’s diplomatic efforts have been muted. Its biggest economic leverage over Iran is the fact that it buys about 90% of the Middle Eastern country’s crude oil exports. Between April and June, it slashed its crude imports by 30%, with the total in June plunging to the lowest level in a decade. That saved the global economy from a major spike in inflation. According to some estimates, China’s cut in oil imports shaved $30 or more off barrel prices of Brent crude, a global benchmark.
Beijing has otherwise done little to broker peace in the Middle East. That is partly because it does not see the conflict as being its responsibility to resolve. In March, Wang said the war “should never have happened” and that the US and Israel would find “no popular support” for the strikes.
China is also a beneficiary from the damage that the fighting has done to the US’s global reputation.
According to findings published in July by the Pew Research Center, a Washington-based thinktank, China is now viewed more favourably than the US in a majority of 36 countries surveyed.
The pain caused by the long-term disruption to the strait of Hormuz, the waterway through which much of the world’s oil and gas flows, also poses a risk to China’s economy. Shortages of energy cause inflation, which risks reducing global demand for Chinese goods.
Tehran and Washington are locked in intensive talks to reach an agreement, which could include reopening the strait. Trump has repeatedly threatened to renew military action against Iran after Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US, a move which would cause alarm in Beijing.
Trump’s desperation to reach a deal in the Middle East may also provide an opportunity for China to present itself as a regional peacemaker, bolstering Xi’s status before their meeting. Beijing brokered a detente between Saudi Arabia and Iran in 2023 but since then its diplomatic impact in the region has been limited.
Shen said China’s desire to improve diplomatic relations with Middle Eastern countries as well as the US were “mutually reinforcing” trends.
China’s foreign ministry spokesperson, Mao Ning, said on Monday that China would send special envoy Zhai Jun to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early to mid-November.

articles.title_orig: Apple announces Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout plans
articles.title_zh: Apple announces Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout plans
articles.content_orig:
Apple wants to help you get stronger. Apple Fitness+ is expanding to the gym with a new strength training experience. Gym Strength is now available in beta, bringing personalized workout plans, exercise demonstrations, and Apple Watch logging to your lifting routine.
Gym Strength creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment. After you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weight you logged.
The feature is designed for a range of experience levels, from people trying strength training for the first time to experienced lifters looking to make progress. It also aims to help anyone who wants to build a more consistent routine.
When building a plan, you choose your workout days and the body areas you want to focus on. You can select five exercises per workout, which Apple estimates will take about 20–30 minutes, or seven exercises for about 45–60 minutes, depending on your pace.
Each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets, and how much weight to lift.
You move through the workout at your own pace, with short video demonstrations from Apple Fitness+ trainers available for each exercise. The demonstrations can be expanded to show the movement from three different angles.
Apple says Gym Strength includes over 350 exercises across more than 30 types of strength training equipment, including dumbbells, kettlebells, suspension trainers, cable machines, and barbells. Dumbbells are the minimum equipment requirement.
Plans account for the equipment available to you, so the experience can work in a commercial gym or a home gym.
If a machine is occupied or you’re training somewhere with different equipment, you can swap equipment or choose an alternative exercise with a similar movement and body focus. You can also add sets or skip exercises.
Gym Strength requires an iPhone running iOS 27.3 or an iPad running iPadOS 27.3. An Apple Watch running watchOS 27.3 optionally lets you view exercises and log reps and weight from your wrist, while tracking heart rate and calories burned.
Gym Strength also introduces Training Note, an optional feature powered by Apple Intelligence that previews workouts, explains progression, and highlights milestones. Training Note requires an Apple Intelligence–enabled iPhone or iPad with the device set to English.
Gym Strength is included in the existing Fitness+ subscription. It joins a library of trainer-led workouts spanning 12 workout types, including Strength, HIIT, Yoga, Pilates, Core, Cycling, Rowing, Dance, Kickboxing, treadmill walking and running, and Mindful Cooldown.
Fitness+ also offers guided meditations, personalized recommendations, and Custom Plans for scheduling workouts, with new sessions added every week .
Apple Fitness+ costs $9.99 per month or $79.99 per year in the U.S., and a subscription can be shared with up to five other family members. New subscribers can try one month free, while eligible device purchases include a three-month trial.
Fitness+ is also included in Apple One Premier, which costs $39.95 per month in the U.S. and bundles Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Arcade, Apple News+, and 2TB of iCloud+ storage.

articles.title_orig: Binance Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews in $6.3 Billion Heist
articles.title_zh: Binance Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews in $6.3 Billion Heist
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Binance has seen $3.64 billion in net outflows since it gradually restored user withdrawals following the largest crypto hack in history, which the FBI linked to North Korea.
The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange said that it processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and approximately $1.01 billion in deposits. Binance detailed that the resulting net outflows represent just 2.1% of its $171 billion in total assets under management.
Binance was hit late Thursday by a hack that investigators said impacted roughly $6.3 billion in funds, with roughly half of those assets frozen.
On Monday, the exchange said it has covered approximately 95% of the impacted amount. The outstanding 5% consists of smaller tokens outside of the top 10 cryptocurrencies, whose assets are less liquid and will take longer to source.
Here's what you need to know:
"We continue working with industry partners to complete the remaining acquisitions," Binance said in an update on X.
Over the weekend, the FBI said the attack was linked to North Korea.
"The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026," a press release said.
Customer withdrawals were temporarily suspended, and co-CEO Richard Teng promised the exchange will cover all losses.
Teng said the hack was not carried out by one person. Initial findings pointed to a compromised laptop, but further review revealed broader security breaches.
"This was a complex attack," Teng said. "The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and tracers."
Around $3.24 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, according to Tom Robinson, chief scientist and co-founder at blockchain analytics company Elliptic.
The attack has rattled crypto markets, and bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) traded at around $77,700 on Monday. Meanwhile, the total crypto market has lost roughly 3% in value, or $80 billion, over the last seven days, according to CoinMarketCap data.
Other major crypto assets also tumbled after the hack, with ether ( ETH-USD ) dropping to roughly $2,200. Binance's native token, BNB ( BND-USD ), also fell.

articles.title_orig: China’s HQ-9B air defense system destroys maneuvering missile in tests
articles.title_zh: China’s HQ-9B air defense system destroys maneuvering missile in tests
articles.content_orig:
Authorities in Beijing announced that the PLA Air Force utilized the HQ-9B surface-to-air missile platform to successfully neutralize targets during a training drill. These objectives consisted of missiles capable of rapid movement and complex maneuvering.
The evaluations of the HQ-9B, a modern addition to the Chinese military inventory, required the interception of two distinct missile varieties. One specific target executed an abrupt mid-air pivot before plummeting toward the earth at extreme velocity.
According to the state media outlet China Central Television (CCTV), the Central Theater Command's Shenwei Missile Battalion within the PLA Air Force carried out the maneuvers.
Personnel from the Shenwei Missile Battalion were not briefed on the specific nature of the incoming threats; they were informed only that the mission involved engaging agile, high-velocity projectiles.
A battalion participant noted that the crew was afforded a mere two-second window to react. In this brief interval, they were required to identify the mysterious object and determine if a launch was necessary.
Military specialist Song Zhongping remarked, in a report by the Global Times , that despite precise radar monitoring, a defense system must possess the capacity for mid-flight trajectory adjustments to successfully follow a target exhibiting erratic flight patterns.
For guidance and tracking during an engagement, the HQ-9B utilizes an active radar homing (ARH) mechanism paired with an inertial navigation system (INS). Beyond its sophisticated steering and engine technologies, the HQ-9B is capable of striking targets that follow non-linear flight paths. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of a missile intercept is contingent upon multiple variables, such as communication reliability, target velocity, reaction speed, and radar precision.
The drill also showcased the PLA's ability to fuse different missile, command, and radar elements into a cohesive air defense web. Expert Song Zhongping clarified that China has established a unified data-sharing architecture for its diverse air defense branches to distribute intelligence on approaching hazards and synchronize their actions. Threats are distributed among various units depending on their proximity and combat readiness.
Hu Yang, another member of the battalion, mentioned that just two minutes elapse between the reception of a high-level warning and the actual interception. While the drill proves the HQ-9B can hit maneuvering missiles, its capacity to stop hypersonic cruise missiles or glide vehicles requires separate validation through authentic combat simulations.
Although the HQ-9B might intercept a target approaching directly, engaging hypersonic cruise missiles or glide vehicles presents an extreme challenge for any surface-to-air hardware. Testing the HQ-9B against maneuvering aerial targets does not verify its effectiveness against operational hypersonic technology. Assessing the system's utility against such weaponry would require distinct trials in practical operational settings.
Earlier, during September 2025, China exhibited numerous air defense assets . Featured hardware included the HQ-29, HQ-19, HQ-9C, and HQ-9B. These platforms represent China's expanding proficiency in defending against diverse missile types and fixed-wing aircraft.
The latest HQ-9B drills highlight the ongoing technical advancement of China's armed forces. Still, the ability of the system to negate sophisticated missile hazards remains unproven until subjected to independent testing in lifelike combat scenarios.

articles.title_orig: Apple releases first iOS 27.3 developer beta for iPhone
articles.title_zh: Apple releases first iOS 27.3 developer beta for iPhone
articles.content_orig:
Apple has released the first iOS 27.3 developer beta for iPhone. The update starts a new round of testing as Apple prepares more features for release later this year.
One change we’re watching for is the return of Apple’s redesigned Health app.
Apple introduced the upgrade during the iOS 27.2 beta cycle before restoring the previous Health app in beta 4.
The company said the new version was still coming later this year, making iOS 27.3 a likely candidate for its return.
The upgrade includes features like Health Age and the ability to schedule lab work through Quest Diagnostics. More on the Health app release timing .
We’ll have to install today’s update and explore what Apple has included before we know the full picture.
For now, iOS 27.3 is available through the developer beta program. We’ll follow up with new features and other changes as we find them.

articles.title_orig: Bomb threats on flights, cruise ship cause disruption in Europe, no devices found
articles.title_zh: Bomb threats on flights, cruise ship cause disruption in Europe, no devices found
articles.content_orig:
At least seven flights and a cruise ship in Europe received bomb threats on Tuesday, causing disruption at airports although no devices were discovered.
At least two flights to Warsaw, two to Sofia, two to ​Rome and one to Murcia airport in Spain were subjected to the threats on Tuesday, and another flight to ‌Sofia had been threatened a day earlier. An airport in Warsaw was briefly shut and the Italian Air Force accompanied one of the flights to Rome while an Israel-bound cruise ship was searched for bombs in Greece.
There was no claim of responsibility and officials did not attribute blame. None of the affected airlines responded to Reuters’ requests for comment.
Rhys Jones, Analysis Output Manager at aviation risk advisory firm Osprey Flight Solutions, ​said that seven confirmed bomb threats in a single day impacting flights was exceptional.
“The lack of clear target state, airline, or route indicates that general ​disruption to aviation operations is the aim,” Jones told Reuters.
Authorities diverted a LOT flight from London that was meant to land at ​Warsaw’s Chopin airport to nearby Modlin airport, which was closed and then reopened after the plane was searched and ​no device was found.
Another Warsaw-bound flight, an SAS flight from Copenhagen, ​landed at Chopin as scheduled. Chopin airport said no device was found and the airport remained operational.
Bomb threats were made against planes traveling from ​Milan/Bergamo and Dublin to Sofia, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters. Both landed safely and no explosive devices were ​found on inspection.
The Bergamo flight was operated by Wizz Air and was carrying 176 passengers, the statement said. The Dublin flight, operated by Ryanair, had 186 passengers on board.
BTA had earlier quoted an Interior Ministry official as saying a flight from Israel had been impacted, but authorities later said this was ​not the case.
A day earlier, a Wizz Air flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Budapest airport after receiving a bomb threat, Hungarian ​Defence Minister ​Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said ⁠in a Facebook post.
In Murcia in southeastern Spain, parts of an airport were cordoned off on Tuesday after a ‌bomb threat ⁠was reported on a Ryanair flight from Manchester.
Officials said the report proved to be a hoax, and the airport resumed normal operations after authorities found no explosives on board. Ryanair declined to immediately comment.
Two other Ryanair flights – one from Lisbon and another from Dublin – were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following bomb threats, said a source from airport operator ADR. The Dublin flight was escorted by the ​Italian Air Force until it landed.
The ​alert was cleared and the ⁠airport continued to operate as usual with no effects on other flights, the person said.
An ⁠explosives detection dog and a diver searched the Panama-flagged Crown Iris cruise ship on the Greek island of Syros after an unknown person said an explosive device had been attached to the boat’s hull, authorities said.
Initial checks found no explosive device with coast ​guard specialists expected to carry out further inspections before the ship could resume its voyage.
While no country pointed fingers over the bomb threats, they come at a time when European officials have been ​blaming both Russia and Iran for what they describe as “hybrid attacks” and acts of sabotage. Moscow ​and Tehran both ⁠deny any such campaign.
This week, unidentified hackers shut down fridges in supermarkets in several European countries. Some experts said hoax bomb threats could be part of a similar pattern of low-cost, deniable disruption efforts.
“From railways to the food infrastructure that you see happening with the fridges being hacked ⁠and all ​kinds of other operations, it does fit the narrative of Russian state actors ​who want to disturb Europe,” said Eric Schouten, the head of aviation security group Dyami.

articles.title_orig: Poland launches major border operation as activity in Russia fuels concern over possible "serious provocation"
articles.title_zh: Poland launches major border operation as activity in Russia fuels concern over possible "serious provocation"
articles.content_orig:
Berlin — Poland launched a large-scale security operation this week along its border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, the country's national police chief said, and the Polish prime minister said the effort may have prevented a sabotage or provocation operation targeting the NATO member.
Additional police and counterterrorism units, as well as troops from the elite military special forces unit GROM, have been deployed as part of the operation, which national police chief Marek Boroń said would run from Monday until at least Nov. 8.
Polish and allied intelligence agencies had warned of possible sabotage operations and provocations during the first half of November, particularly along Poland's border with Kaliningrad, and including possible border incursions by armed groups.
Those warnings had already put domestic security agencies on high alert even before the additional security forces were deployed to the northeast regions of Warmia-Masuria and Podlaskie.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Tuesday that suspicious movements were observed overnight near Kaliningrad, including individuals carrying flashlights close to the border area.
He said the quick reaction by Polish security forces may have prevented an unspecified provocation this week.
"We very quickly mobilized the necessary security forces and means on site, and we successfully prevented any attempted acts of provocation, if that was the intention. Of course, we will never be able to completely confirm that," Tusk said Tuesday, adding that intelligence had pointed for weeks to possible "acts of diversion or more serious provocation" against the European Union, including "the intrusion of armed individuals into Polish territory."
A special command center was set up at Polish national police headquarters to coordinate the new security operation.
The goal is to protect the public, detect suspicious activities early, and prevent attacks on critical infrastructure, the police said Tuesday.
Russia's exclave of Kaliningrad, bordered only by NATO members Poland and Lithuania and the Baltic Sea to the west, is of considerable military and strategic significance. It is widely believed that Russian security agencies, including the FSB and GRU intelligence agencies, have a presence in the territory in eastern Europe.
To the immediate east of Kaliningrad is the strategically important Suwałki Corridor — the only land border connecting the Baltic NATO states with the rest of the alliance, where Poland and Lithuania share a short border sandwiched between Russian and Belarusian territory.
Polish authorities had not published any evidence of specific plans for an act of sabotage or an attack originating from Kaliningrad by Tuesday afternoon, but the alert comes after months of sabotage, air incursion and other low-level incidents across Europe blamed largely on Russia.
During a joint news conference with Lithuania's prime minister on Oct. 13, Tusk referred to a conversation he had recently had with NATO Supreme Allied Commander Alexus Grynkewich, and said it had reinforced his own concerns about increasing threats of sabotage, including possible provocations involving aircraft or attacks on border crossings.
At about the same time, the head of Britain's domestic spy agency MI5, Sir Ken McCallum, painted a dark picture of the security threats facing the U.K. and Europe, and he said that among state threats, "Russia remains aggressor number one."
"The Russian military and intelligence services are once again escalating their attempts at hybrid warfare," McCallum warned, adding that Moscow was "being careful to stay below the NATO Article 5 threshold" with its actions, which would trigger the alliance's collective defense principle .
"It'd be foolish for them to cross" that line, he said, and so far Russia was sticking to "tactics that stop short — though sometimes not much short — of conventional conflict."
Among the numerous incidents attributed to Russia across Europe this year alone, there was a fire in August at a Polish factory that produces drones and other military components, and an arson attack on a Starlink satellite ground station that Polish officials blamed directly on Russia in September.
Russian drones have also crossed into NATO airspace in Eastern Europe repeatedly during the war in Ukraine , and just this week the U.K. Royal Navy said it had intercepted a Russian spy ship off the far northern coast of Scotland.
The navy said helicopters were dispatched to track the intelligence-gathering ship, which was "closely monitoring" a NATO exercise taking place near Scotland's Outer Hebrides islands.

articles.title_orig: S&P 500, Nasdaq rise as tech stocks gain ahead of midterm results
articles.title_zh: S&P 500, Nasdaq rise as tech stocks gain ahead of midterm results
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Noel Randewich and Utkarsh Hathi
Nov 3 (Reuters) - The Nasdaq rallied on Tuesday as AI heavyweights rebounded ahead of US midterm election results, while Apple fell after the iPhone maker joined the list of Big Tech companies whose quarterly ‌results failed to impress investors.
Apple dropped 1.8% after it warned that the cost of memory chips would continue to ‌rise, pressuring its holiday-quarter gross margin.
Memory-chip maker Micron Technology added 2.1%, while Nvidia climbed 3% after falling in the last four sessions.
The broader Philadelphia chips index jumped almost ​3%, while AMD gained 5.5% ahead of its quarterly earnings due after the bell.
Microsoft and Amazon each gained about 2%.
"This is a rotation from safe tech, like Apple, into riskier tech, like chipmakers," said Jay Hatfield, chief executive officer at Infrastructure Capital Management. "It's clear dip-buying in a higher-risk, Nasdaq-driven market."
The Nasdaq-100 on Monday ended more than 10% below its October 6 record-high close, confirming that the tech-heavy index has entered a ‌correction as investors worry that massive investments in ⁠AI infrastructure are outpacing near-term cash generation.
Shares of Amazon and Alphabet fell sharply last week after their quarterly results deepened investors' concerns about the cost of heavy AI spending.
The S&P 500 is down about 3% ⁠from its record-high close on October 6, and it remains up 11% in 2026.
Oil prices slid about 2% to a three-week low as investors weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries about additional supply disruptions from recent attacks in both conflicts. Iran and the United ​States ​are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior ​Iranian official told Reuters.
The S&P 500 was up 0.59% ‌at 7,585.95 points.
The Nasdaq jumped 1.06% to 25,431.03 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.24% at 51,859.84 points.
Six of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by information technology, up 1.49%, followed by a 1.24% gain in industrials.
Gartner dropped 13.6%, while US-listed shares of Thomson Reuters and Shopify fell 7.1% and 4.8%, respectively, after all three reported quarterly results.
AI-powered analytics software provider Palantir Technologies forecast revenue above estimates for the last three months of the year after topping third-quarter expectations. Its shares fell 1.1%, however.
American voters will deliver a verdict on the first two years of President ​Donald Trump's second term in Tuesday's midterm elections, with polls and nonpartisan analysts ​favoring Democrats to wrest the House from Republicans, while control ​of the Senate remains uncertain.
"Markets will assess potential implications for fiscal policy, regulation, taxation and government spending. This ‌will be good to put behind us as it ​has been an anticipated volatility event ​for quite some time," said Ken Mahoney, CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.
Morgan Stanley analysts said in a note earlier this week that the elections should help remove a major market overhang. They believe a US market correction that began in June ​is in its "final innings."
Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones ‌within the S&P 500 by a 1.3-to-one ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 10 new highs and one new low; the ​Nasdaq recorded 48 new highs and 197 new lows.
(Reporting by Noel Randewich in San Francisco and Shashwat Chauhan and ​Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel and Matthew Lewis)

articles.title_orig: Google dismantles botnet secretly running on 1.3 million Android TV boxes
articles.title_zh: Google dismantles botnet secretly running on 1.3 million Android TV boxes
articles.content_orig:
Google’s Threat Intelligence Group says it has shut down a massive botnet called x.cpe. At its height, x.cpe ran on more than 1.3 million Android TV devices, and unusually, these were Google-certified boxes. Google says its screening process missed the malware due to “obfuscation techniques” employed by Shenzhen-based Videostrong Technology.
In a detailed blog post , the Threat Intelligence Group explains how the x.cpe botnet evolved quickly from a single-stage dropper into a modular three-stage malware platform that sold access to third parties. Manufacturers must have their devices certified if they want access to Google apps and branding, a process that is supposed to catch threats like this. However, Videostrong’s compromised boxes, mostly sold under the MECOOL brand, evaded detection by using a backdoor to remotely install the malware after the devices were set up and online.
After devices appeared online, a stub application called x.cpe or com.oemservice would phone home. This package did not have any malicious capabilities of its own, but it had the system-level permissions necessary to install malware modules at the operator’s behest. It also disabled Play Protect, which would have otherwise flagged the silently installed packages as malicious.
Google found most of the boxes were running residential proxies for routing large volumes of nefarious traffic or modules that engaged in ad fraud schemes. Selling access to this botnet was probably a big business. Videostrong also had full access to the devices, allowing operators to run terminal commands, capture the screen, and probe other devices on the local network. Google reportedly observed Videostrong doing this in real time.
Google worked with several other organizations to disrupt the x.cpe network, including Japan’s National Police Agency, Synthient, and Trend Micro. Google says it has taken legal action to shut down the domains and servers Videostrong used to operate and install its malware. It also went after command-and-control servers operated by Videostrong that were connected to other malware campaigns. Google estimates Videostrong has been cut off from about 10 million compromised devices.
This action should make the affected devices safe to use, but probably not as safe as they should be. Play Protect is still disabled, and the inert malware modules are still installed. Since they are loaded as system apps, users cannot easily remove them.
Synthient has published a list of 182 device model names known to be included in the botnet. Anyone who has purchased a MECOOL or white label Android TV box of unknown origin should check it. Trend Micro counted a total of 1,472,554 infected devices, somewhat higher than Google’s estimate. The overwhelming majority were in Brazil, Malaysia, Iraq, Mexico, and Taiwan, but tens of thousands were also online in the US, Germany, the UK, Australia, and Canada.
Google determined the operation was not the work of a rogue actor, so it has ended its relationship with Videostrong. The company, as well as any subsidiaries, will not be permitted to use Google’s Android apps and services.
Google also notes that it is updating its certification process to close the loophole that allowed Videostrong to operate its botnet on certified devices. Android is open source, though, and there are countless uncertified Android-based TV boxes out there. Videostrong could continue to sell malicious hardware under other brands without Google apps. But it would still have to rebuild its malware operation from scratch.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute
articles.title_zh: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute
articles.content_orig:

There’s a lot of mystery around the finances of major AI labs, and as Anthropic inches towards it IPO, we’re starting to get some answers. In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs.
In a new filing on Monday , Anthropic released data that showed those margins on compute actually getting worse. The filing was an update to the S-1 released last week — but where that filing’s financial disclosures only covered through June 30 of this year, the new data extended to disclose results through an extra quarter, to September 30. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth. But the operating loss grew at the same time, thanks in large part to growing compute costs.
Looking at the compute margins makes the picture even worse. In the new quarter, compute took up 58% of the company’s revenue, up from 48% the quarter before. At a moment when the company could win over IPO investors by showing margins improving, they’re getting worse.
A chart in the filing shows this even more clearly, tracking the company’s revenue for every dollar spent on compute. Since the start of 2025, it’s been steadily growing, peaking at just over 2x this past quarter, then falling back down to 1.72x.
Many indications imply that this shift in compute margins is more of a blip than a long-term problem, but it still tells us important things about the business of running a major lab. Trying to keep up with demand, Anthropic’s compute bill shot up to $10 billion for the quarter, including, as the filing notes, “$5.0 billion of compute under short-term commitments, which currently costs significantly more than comparable compute procured under our multi-year commitments.” Basically, demand was growing so fast that Anthropic had to scramble for compute, which meant paying higher rates.
Some of those deals have already played out in public. Anthropic has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute, alongside multibillion-dollar deals with Nscale , Akamai , and Volta . In the parlance of the industry, these are neoclouds rather than hyperscalers — smaller outfits that offer more flexible compute deals at higher rates.
Anthropic’s margins got worse in Q3 because of deals like these, and there’s no sign they’ll be able to do without them anytime soon. As the new filing puts it, “We expect compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain our largest operating expense for the foreseeable future as additional committed compute becomes available to us under multi-year arrangements with CSPs, and as we continue to invest in additional compute.”
Anthropic is still trying to lower its compute costs. In particular, the company talks quite a bit about its efforts to build its own compute base under a project it calls “Anthropic Direct.” But with demand growing so fast, those efforts aren’t going to be able to keep pace, and the neoclouds will continue to be the best option they have.
In a sense, these are champagne problems. As long as revenue is growing at nearly 50% a quarter, few investors will worry about high compute costs — and the moment demand slows down, investors may be comforted by a compute picture that has gotten a lot sunnier. But it’s a reminder of how much AI labs still depend on the trillion-dollar infrastructure buildout — and how vulnerable they are to hiccups in that process. It’s easy to imagine the data center buildout slowing down over the next year if bond markets get skittish or local opposition gets more intense. There’s not much Anthropic can do to address either of those risks, and either one would make a messy compute picture a whole lot messier.
In the meantime, the future of Anthropic and other labs will be at the mercy of compute prices.

articles.title_orig: King calls slave trade a 'shameful chapter' during Commonwealth address
articles.title_zh: King calls slave trade a 'shameful chapter' during Commonwealth address
articles.content_orig:
King Charles has described the transatlantic slave trade as a "shameful chapter of history" that filled him with "profound sorrow" as he opened a summit of Commonwealth leaders in the Caribbean.
He said the trade in enslaved persons "still casts a shadow" over the association of nations.
There has been calls from some for the UK to make a formal apology for its historic role in the slave trade ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm) in Antigua and Barbuda, but there was not one in the King's address.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who is also at the summit, has previously said he is open to Britain issuing a formal apology but that financial reparations were "not the right answer".
While there was no direct apology, the King did offer some contrition - and there was also an acknowledgement that he had personally learnt more about the legacy of the slave trade.
He said: "The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth.
"As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow."
He told the summit: "The more I have furthered my own understanding of the issues, through listening, learning and looking, the more committed I have become to finding ways for us to work in modern partnership to address the wrongs of the past with action for the future."
King Charles continued: "History is not ours to choose or to change. It is bequeathed to us in complex synthesis by forebears we can never know.
"Our inheritance includes both their achievements and their failures – the good they did as well as the wrongs."
The King's address also referenced the "brutal conflicts" the world is facing, the "catastrophic reality" of climate and rapid technological development.
The Chogm meeting gathers leaders from 56 states every two years in a different part of the Commonwealth, a voluntary grouping made up primarily of former territories of the British Empire.
The biennial meeting's official theme this year is Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.
The King and Queen are on a tour of the Caribbean which has reignited difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.
On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech in which he spoke of the "suffering of the past".
In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion, where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

articles.title_orig: With World of Warcraft: Forever, Blizzard had to reconnect with what made WoW great in the first place
articles.title_zh: With World of Warcraft: Forever, Blizzard had to reconnect with what made WoW great in the first place
articles.content_orig:
A lot of the team had to "unlearn" design habits they picked over the years.
After 13 years at Blizzard, Michael Nuthals faces what might just be the toughest challenge of his career yet: working on a familiar but different and highly anticipated version of World of Warcraft . As lead encounter designer, he's part of the team working on WoW: Forever . Announced at BlizzCon earlier this year, Forever is a sort of remaster of WoW designed to expand on the game's "Classic" era . It takes players back to Azeroth, the setting of the original 2004 game, before Blizzard over the course of 11 expansions took the game in the direction that it did. In the process, it imagines a "what if" scenario.
What if Blizzard had continued to expand Azeroth, instead of sending players to the Orc homeworld of Draenor and beyond with The Burning Crusade and later expansions? In Forever , there are more than 1,000 new quests for players to complete, many of them designed to continue story threads that were left unresolved in the original game. Additionally, there are new areas within Azeroth for players to explore — including Mount Hyjal, the site of one of Warcraft III 's pivotal battles — in addition to fresh dungeons and raids. Blizzard has also rebalanced the game's classes and items, and built an entirely new global illumination lighting pipeline to make the game feel more atmospheric. Controversially, Forever will also feature a new race, the Skyborne Elves, who weren't in the original game.
The challenge Nuthals and his colleagues face is one of expectations. Nearly right from the moment Blizzard rereleased the original World of Warcraft in 2019 , players have been asking the studio for a "Classic+" experience that expands the original game. The tricky thing is that, before Forever's announcement, every player had a different opinion on what an expanded rerelease should look like. Seemingly the only consensus was that the game shouldn't play anything like modern "retail" WoW . Realistically, there was never going to be a way Blizzard would find a way to please everyone with Forever , but it's still trying to create something fans both old and new can appreciate.
"I see it more as an opportunity — an opportunity to engage, to listen and show that we're listening," Nuthals says when asked about the weight of those expectations. With Forever , Blizzard recently concluded the largest beta in World of Warcraft's history . This is despite the fact players had to purchase one of Forever's premium bundles, which start at $60, to take part in the experience. Nuthals says Blizzard received "a lot of feedback" during the beta. He later admits one of the challenges of making Forever has been letting go of habits he learned working on the current version of WoW .
"Some of us had worked on the modern game for a long time, myself included. I come from modern, and it's almost like unlearning what you have learned," said Nuthals, who began working full-time on WoW ahead of 2014's Warlords of Draenor expansion. "We needed to understand what the DNA was [of WoW Classic ], what the philosophies were, and to do that you just had to put it under your fingers and play." One way Nuthals and his colleagues did that was by revisiting the original game each week. Every Thursday morning, he and the rest of the encounter team would replay a classic dungeon like The Deadmines before jumping into one of the new dungeons they've created for Forever , such as Ruins of Lordaeron . Afterwards, they would ask themselves if those two dungeons felt like "they could live hand in glove?" and were connected.
"That was the development process," explains Nuthals. "We thought about what we want Forever to feel like, and we wanted it to feel like you wouldn't even know — like it was made in 2004. That was the vibe we were going for." Nuthals also credits the work Blizzard did with Season of Discovery , which was an offshoot of WoW Classic that saw the studio experiment with new class abilities, progression systems and dungeons within the confines of the original game.
"With Season of Discovery, we were pushing boundaries, exploring what Classic encounters could be. For Forever , we really looked back at the original Classic encounters and wanted to capture those, so we could provide a really authentic and nostalgic experience as players do these new raids," Nuthals said. As part of that process, the one thing he and the team kept coming back to is something Nuthals describes as the "strength, dexterity and intelligence" triangle of encounter design. Strength encounters reward the player for all the gear they've accumulated and their skill with their class, while dexterity ones test how well they can move and avoid hazards. Finally, intelligence-focused encounters test your understanding of a fight's mechanics and how much planning you've done.
"What we're trying to do with raids and dungeons is move toward gearing and planning, because Classic players really love that," said Nuthals. "'I overprepare, then I come in and crush the content.' That was the vibe we really wanted to hit." Part of how that philosophy will play out involves Forever 's much advertised "horizontal" progression. With the new game, the studio has said it plans to keep the level cap at 60, meaning there won't be massive jumps in player power when the studio drops major new content. On paper at least, Blizzard appears committed to rewarding those who engage with and explore the game deeply.
"We're seeding the world with all these new items and things to chase, and in the future, having one of those items might pay off," said Nuthals. "We're thinking about those opportunities as we architect future raids and decide what bosses to introduce: making sure you feel smart for having pocketed something that comes in handy later. It feels good to use all that cool gear you went out and got."
Nuthals also said in the future Blizzard hopes to add new dungeons and zones, and that "not all of them will be max level." He added "there are areas players know about and want to explore, and there are opportunities for us to tell new stories in this space — taking what might have been a one-off quest name or something you found on a piece of paper and developing that story."
One question I didn't get a chance to ask Nuthals is what Blizzard will do if players, upon reaching 60, drop Forever and move onto other games. It's one thing for a studio to say it's committed to doing things differently with an MMO that doesn't take prey on player FOMO, and an entirely different thing to actually stick to that philosophy. We'll see how the future of Forever starts to unfold when the game arrives on November 4 .

articles.title_orig: Windows 11 is now ‘up to 40 percent faster’ on PCs with 8GB of RAM
articles.title_zh: Windows 11 is now ‘up to 40 percent faster’ on PCs with 8GB of RAM
articles.content_orig:
A new Windows 11 update is improving memory usage and performance.
A new Windows 11 update is improving memory usage and performance.
Microsoft has been doing a lot of work to improve memory usage and increase performance on Windows 11 PCs over the past year. Last month the company revealed Windows 11 is now “more responsive” and runs better on PCs with 8GB of RAM, and now the company is releasing a new update today that includes further memory improvements.
“On 8 GB PCs, Windows is now up to 20 percent more responsive, and multitasking is up to 40 percent faster in our lab test,” says Windows chief Pavan Davuluri . One of the key ways Microsoft has achieved better performance on PCs with 8GB of RAM is through compression.
“As a result, Windows can now keep up to 2 GB more of your active data in memory instead of moving it to slower storage, so an app or tab you left open is less likely to reload when you return,” says Davuluri. This compression helps Windows avoid writing data to a virtual memory paging file on a disk, slowing down apps and performance.
Microsoft is also making improvements across Windows, Edge, and Microsoft 365 apps that reduce “committed-memory growth by up to 900 MB.” Memory improvements in Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook alone add up to 360MB of RAM savings. Windows 11 no longer loads widgets on a PC with 8GB of RAM until you open the widgets panel, saving around 200MB of RAM. Inactive tabs in Edge now sleep after 15 minutes, reducing memory consumption further.
While Microsoft is shipping an update to Windows 11 with these memory improvements, the company is still working on improving RAM usage in Windows in the coming months. Memory compression will get “smarter and more efficient” over the next few months, and Windows features and apps will share more common parts like widgets and search sharing a single web engine. Microsoft is also working with PC makers and chipmakers to optimize how much memory a PC needs to reserve for its hardware, enabling more for Windows.

articles.title_orig: Xbox’s smallest-ever controller is surprisingly comfortable
articles.title_zh: Xbox’s smallest-ever controller is surprisingly comfortable
articles.content_orig:
The Nano controller is designed for young people, anyone with smaller hands, and gaming on the go.
The Nano controller is designed for young people, anyone with smaller hands, and gaming on the go.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
Even though I knew Microsoft’s new Xbox Nano controller was tiny, I still gasped when I unboxed it a few days ago. The compact controller is small enough to slip into a pocket unnoticed, and it has been designed specifically for younger people, or for anyone with smaller hands.
I’m not young, but I do have small hands, and I’ve been surprised at how comfortable the Nano is during gaming sessions. At just over 5 inches long, almost everything on this controller has been shrunk down somehow. The ABXY buttons are ever so slightly smaller than a regular Xbox controller, and the thumbsticks feel like miniature versions. Microsoft hasn’t changed the D-pad, though, or the size of the glowing Xbox button at the center of the controller.
The big difference I noticed with the Nano over a regular Xbox controller was the size of the triggers. While they are fully analog and pressure sensitive, they have more of a click when you bottom them out compared with the thud on a bigger Xbox controller. They’re noticeably smaller, as you’d expect, and the bumper buttons above the triggers feel less clicky than the regular ones.
I thought the Nano controller would feel awkward after a few hours of gaming, but the grips really help with comfort levels — a lot of smaller controllers sacrifice grips to keep the controller thin and lightweight. It does mean the Nano doesn’t sit flush on a table, but at 101 grams (0.22 pounds) it’s still really lightweight.
I can’t speak for those with bigger hands, but I’d expect the Nano controller won’t be well-suited to everyone. The size makes it ideal for young children, though. I tried to get my 1-year-old son to try the Nano, and he responded with a smile, so I guess he likes it.
I haven’t had enough time to get a full idea of battery life yet, but it seems to drain around 10 percent in around 30 to 40 minutes. That suggests a lot less battery life than the 30 hours you’d get on a rechargeable pack for the larger Xbox wireless controller. Thankfully, the Nano charges quickly, and I found I could get from 30 percent to 60 percent charge in less than 10 minutes. You can plug in a USB-C charger to top up the battery and carry on playing while you charge.
The only thing missing on the Nano controller that I would have loved is vibration support. I assume it’s not there because of an impact on battery life, because even the smaller Nintendo Joy-Con controllers have rumble support.
The Xbox Nano controller will be available on November 4th, priced at $49.99 .

articles.title_orig: Outback Steakhouse franchisee files for bankruptcy
articles.title_zh: Outback Steakhouse franchisee files for bankruptcy
articles.content_orig:
California Pizza Kitchen co-founder Rick Rosenfield told Fox News Digital how two former prosecutors built a pizza empire and how he believes the iconic chain is moving towards a 'new glory.'
Outback Steakhouse parent company Bloomin' Brands is moving to acquire 61 restaurants operated by a major franchisee that filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.
Out West Restaurant Group, which operates Outback Steakhouse locations across the western United States, filed for bankruptcy protection in Delaware on Monday, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Bloomin' Brands has entered into an agreement to purchase Out West's assets for approximately $26.3 million, subject to certain adjustments and the assumption of specified liabilities.
MCDONALD'S DEALT LEGAL SETBACK AS JUDGE ALLOWS MCRIB MEAT LAWSUIT TO PROCEED
Outback Steakhouse (iStock)
The company is expected to serve as the "stalking-horse" bidder in the bankruptcy sale process, establishing an initial offer that other potential buyers can seek to exceed. The transaction remains subject to bankruptcy court approval.
Bloomin' Brands also agreed to provide up to $5.5 million in interest-free debtor-in-possession financing to support Out West's operations during the Chapter 11 proceedings, subject to court approval.
Customers enter an Outback Steakhouse restaurant at the Queens Place Mall in the Queens borough of New York, U.S., on Friday, Nov. 9, 2012. (Getty Images)
Out West intends to continue operating its restaurants throughout the bankruptcy process, according to the SEC filing.
Bloomin' Brands said the filing would have no immediate impact on customers, restaurant employees or daily operations at the affected Outback Steakhouse locations.
The bankruptcy involves restaurants operated by the franchisee rather than Bloomin' Brands' corporate-owned locations.
Outback Steakhouse location (Getty Images)
Out West is affiliated with Cerca Trova Restaurant Group, which has operated Outback Steakhouse restaurants across several western states, including California, Arizona, Nevada, Colorado and New Mexico .
The proposed acquisition could bring the franchisee-operated restaurants under Bloomin' Brands' control if the company prevails in the court-supervised sale process.

Bloomin' Brands also owns Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar.

articles.title_orig: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
articles.title_zh: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
articles.content_orig:
Russian strikes on Ukraine – including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital – have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others over the last 24 hours.
At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble.
He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war".
Ukraine had proposed to extend and expand last week's ceasefire in the Kherson region which allowed people from the frontline Russian-occupied town of Oleshky to evacuate, Zelensky added.
The attack on a school building being used as an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha was Moscow's response, he said.
Elsewhere, a hospice was attacked in the central city of Dnipro and a hospital was hit in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly patients.
Nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit Komyshuvakha as residents were gathering to receive humanitarian aid at a distribution centre, authorities said. Local media reported that when the attack began, people took refuge underground but the roof  collapsed, trapping many underneath.
"The scale of the tragedy is difficult to comprehend," regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
Russia's defense ministry said the attack had targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen.
However, there was no credible evidence that the site was being used by the Ukrainian military and there were no major military or industrial facilities in the settlement of Komyshuvakha, reports BBC News Russian defence correspondent Ilya Abishev.
The village is to the south-east of the city of Zaporizhzhia, which has come under constant Russian bombardment.
According to Abishev, Komyshuvakha is of high military importance as part of Ukraine's defensive and transport network on the approaches to the regional capital.
But the UN's human rights monitoring mission said the distribution of humanitarian aid at the local school had been highly publicised and the attack "seems to have violated the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law" .
Further north, in Dnipro, nearly 50 terminally ill patients were being transferred to other facilities after their hospice was destroyed by a Russian missile on Monday night. The oldest of the patients was 90 years old.
Mayor Boris Filatov posted photos on Telegram showing elderly people lying in their beds in a hospice room with blown-out windows and rubble and broken glass strewn on the floors.
"I realise that I am violating ethics," wrote Filatov. "I want as many people as possible to see these photos. Especially politicians and diplomats. Especially abroad.
"These are elderly, terminally ill people. This is a Russian missile."
Elsewhere in Dnipro, a separate strike killed two people and left 18 others wounded. Another five people were killed in aerial bomb and drone strikes on Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region.
Russia has also struck energy infrastructure in nine regions, affecting water and heating.
The water supply in Kyiv was entirely cut off "due to enemy attacks and damage to the capital's energy infrastructure", the main water supplier Kyivvodokanal said. The entire metro network was suspended on Tuesday and Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the situation surrounding the city's power supply was becoming "very difficult".
As Ukraine was counting its dead, the Kremlin announced it would take part in three-way peace talks with Ukraine brokered by the US in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November.
It will be the first trilateral meeting since February. Since then, Russia and the US have begun engaging more directly, with US President Donald Trump announcing a deal to import Russian diesel.
Speaking to reporters in Berlin on Tuesday, Zelensky said that it was important for Russia to engage seriously in negotiations on a ceasefire and a peaceful settlement, but that he had so far had not seen "any indication" of that being the case.
Several rounds of ceasefire talks late last year yielded no results, and in public declarations Russian officials have generally refused to budge from Moscow's maximalist demand of effective Ukrainian surrender.
US First Lady Melania Trump Melania Trump, who was credited with brokering a truce last week in the besieged town of Oleshky, is set to host representatives of Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday. However, no details were given in the White House statement of who was due to attend the meeting.
The UN said last month that civilian casualties in Ukraine had reached a "record level", as Russian armed forces resumed systematic attacks on energy infrastructure.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its advances on the front line have since stalled, and attacks on Ukraine have intensified, with Moscow employing large numbers of missiles and drones to strike Ukrainian cities.
At the same time, Ukraine is faces a critical air defense shortage due to stalled Western deliveries of weapons and a lack of American Patriot interceptor missiles.
In Berlin, Zelensky acknowledged that although the front line was stable "the situation in the air was not as positive, particularly when it comes to our air defence capabilities and the protection of our civilian population".

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: US billionaire leads swap plan to buy Lukoil's overseas assets, sources say
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: US billionaire leads swap plan to buy Lukoil's overseas assets, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Todd Boelli's consortium is preparing a transaction to take over the Russian giant's oil fields, refineries and gas stations abroad, with a deal expected in the coming weeks.
A consortium led by US billionaire Todd Boely is preparing a securities exchange to take over the international assets of sanctioned Russian oil giant Lukoil, with a deal expected in the coming weeks, four people familiar with the sale process said.
A bank acting on behalf of the consortium has purchased billions of dollars worth of frozen Lukoil securities from Western investment funds, which would be exchanged for the company's foreign assets, three sources said.
The sources asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly on the matter.
If completed, the transaction would mark the end of a sales process that has lasted more than a year, in which the value of the offered assets was initially estimated at $22 billion.
Lukoil's foreign assets include oil fields, refineries and gas stations in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
The value of that portfolio has since declined as some facilities have ceased operations, two sources said.
An eventual deal would also be a test of the ability of Western sanctions to force a major Russian company to sell international assets, while preserving strategic oil operations and limiting financial benefits for Moscow.
The consortium consists of Boeli, a Miami-based businessman who has ownership stakes in Los Angeles sports clubs, the Dodgers and the Lakers, as well as investors from the United Arab Emirates - International Holding Company (IHC) and Al Hail Holding.
The bid is also supported by the Syrian-Qatari Al Hayat brothers, as well as the American International Development Finance Corporation (DFC).
Boeli's representatives did not respond to multiple requests for comment. An IHC spokesperson said they do not comment on potential investment activities.
Al Hail Companies, Al Hayat Brothers and the US DFC also did not respond to requests for comment.
Lukoil did not respond to a request for comment.
Among the Western investors whose securities are included in the planned transaction is Capital Group, which declined to comment.
The sale process began after the US imposed sanctions on Lukoil in October 2025.
Reuters reported in February that the US had slowed sales, partly to pressure Russia during negotiations to end the war in Ukraine.
More than a dozen companies were bidding for Lukoil's assets, including oil giants Exxon Mobil and Chevron, US investment firm Carlyle and former Pornhub owner Bernd Bergmayr, Reuters reported in November last year.
Carlyle withdrew from the race last month, bringing the Boeli-led consortium to the forefront.
A bank acting on behalf of the consortium bought Lukoil securities from a dozen US and British investment funds, as well as from US depository banks that held them on behalf of small investors, two sources said.
The shares were purchased at 30 cents for every dollar of their value, two other sources said, a significant discount reflecting the fact that they are under sanctions.
Western investment funds were large owners of Lukoil shares before the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
The shares were subsequently removed from the main emerging market stock indices, and Western funds have meanwhile frozen them and reduced their book value.
